PullRequest.Title: eslint: enable no bracket notation rule
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- enable `local/code-no-bracket-notation-for-identifiers` for JavaScript and TypeScript files
- grandfather the 509 files containing 3,550 existing violations in a sorted external allowlist
- protect additions to the allowlist with CODEOWNERS review by `@alexdima` and `@dmitrivMS`

The companion test coverage is in #334753.

## Validation

- verified the allowlist exactly matches the lint audit: 509 expected paths, 509 entries, no duplicates, missing paths, or extra paths
- verified the rule is enabled for a new unlisted TypeScript file
- verified the rule is not configured for an allowlisted baseline file
- `npm run eslint` — checked 11,925 files successfully
- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts .github/CODEOWNERS eslint.config.js .eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`

Full `npm run hygiene` remains blocked on Windows by the existing `C:\C:\...\remote\package.json` URL-path resolution issue, unrelated to these changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Full-repository ESLint in pull-request and product-quality CI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ESLint must load the flat config, discover/read source files, parse them, run enabled visitors, and format results before the hygiene job completes. The added allowlist read and rule visitor are on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously read and split .eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files while loading eslint.config.js.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small 554-line file read per ESLint config evaluation/worker, independent of source-file count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The config synchronously read .eslint-ignore and .eslint-allowed-javascript-files; it did not read this third allowlist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks that worker's lint configuration startup before files can be linted, but is bounded and comparable to the two existing synchronous configuration-file reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and read repository JavaScript/TypeScript lint targets through ESLint.lintFiles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository-wide lint set, with file reads governed by ESLint's content cache and worker scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ESLint already enumerated, read, parsed, and linted the same target patterns with many local rules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing work dominates the lint job; the diff adds a lightweight AST visitor to non-allowlisted files but does not add per-node filesystem calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Repository lint targets; the new config excludes the 509 grandfathered files, then visits each MemberExpression in the remaining JavaScript/TypeScript ASTs. TypeScript scanner creation is further limited to computed, unescaped string-literal properties, whose baseline effective cardinality is intentionally near zero because files with existing violations are excluded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: build/eslint.ts uses ESLint concurrency 'auto', so source files are processed by ESLint workers. Config initialization, including the added synchronous allowlist read, may occur once in each worker; there is no newly added unbounded task fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ESLint uses the content cache at .eslintcache. Cold runs parse and lint all targets; warm runs can reuse unchanged-file results, although config matching/loading still occurs. The allowlist is static configuration and introduces no application cache, negative cache, or invalidation lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed execution path and cardinality: the config entry is repository-wide, its 509 exact-path ignores are explicit, the rule's guards precede scanner creation, and the lint driver uses content caching plus automatic worker concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact config-pattern matching and visitor timing was not benchmarked, but the changed I/O and scanner cardinalities are structurally bounded; no evidence supports a material CI latency or resource regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added filesystem read is constant and small; AST traversal is folded into the existing ESLint traversal, and expensive TypeScript scanner creation occurs only for the rare candidate syntax outside grandfathered files.

Scenarios.Scenario: Targeted ESLint invocation for one or a few changed files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Config load and the requested files' lint passes must complete before the command returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the new allowlist during config import, then read explicitly requested lint files on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One allowlist read per config evaluation plus at most the small requested target set on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Targeted lint loaded the existing config files and read requested source files, without the additional allowlist read or bracket-notation visitor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The allowlist read is on startup, but remains a constant small operation; target reads were already required.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The explicit target count and MemberExpression count within those files; the rule creates a scanner only for computed unescaped string-literal property accesses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ESLint controls concurrency with 'auto'; for a small target set, effective parallelism is bounded by the requested files and its worker implementation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Content-cache hits can skip unchanged target analysis. Config loading and the one small allowlist read remain fixed overhead per worker/process.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added work executes; high confidence that it is bounded for targeted linting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured startup delta is available, but the fixed 554-line read and bounded syntax checks do not establish meaningful latency impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because the added constant startup I/O and per-candidate CPU are too small and bounded to establish concrete degraded latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build-script unit test suite executing the new RuleTester cases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The build test process imports the new test and rule, then synchronously runs the finite valid and invalid parser/fixer cases before the suite completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the added test module and its imported ESLint/rule modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One module load per test worker/process and 11 in-memory RuleTester cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The build test suite did not contain these 11 RuleTester cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded test-suite CPU/module-loading time only; no runtime product path is affected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly the 11 added test snippets in this file; there is no data-dependent or repository-sized loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node's test runner controls file-level test concurrency; this test adds no explicit concurrency, queue, or subprocess.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Module loading follows Node's per-process module cache, so the rule module is imported once per test process.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete added test file and build/package.json test glob.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual parser-test duration is not measured, but case count is fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the finite test coverage adds only bounded development/CI work and no scaling mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review over all five changed files and every diff page. Traced repository-wide and targeted lint execution plus the new unit-test path, including filesystem boundaries, caching, and worker concurrency. The PR adds a constant allowlist read and a guarded AST visitor, with no high-confidence actionable performance regression and no evidenced shipped regression fix.
